headline: Sell long term; lacks scale and competitive positioning versus Medibank; unsustainable cost pressures and younger demographic lapsing coverage
reasoning: Andrew D'Alfin argued the entire health insurance sector faces unsustainable cost inflation and rising premiums are pushing younger consumers to lapse coverage. Despite trading at only 13-14x earnings he would rather not be exposed to this industry structurally.
quote: They've done a great job over the years, but they probably lack a bit of scale, they lack a bit of competitive positioning. And and I think it's just going to be really hard. Premiums are going to go up. They're going to be able to offset some of those rising costs. But something like a Medibank, which is just that much bigger and that much well better placed in this environment is probably going to do better. headline: Prime Value holds NIB Health as an attractively priced quality business despite near-term margin pressure from elective surgery recovery
reasoning: NIB is a large private health insurer that benefited from lower claims during COVID ('covid winner'), generating very high cashflows. headline: Prime Value initiated a position in NIB Holdings in April, viewing it as a high-quality private health insurer trading at a significant valuation discount to the market
reasoning: NIB Holdings is a relatively well-known Australian private health insurer focused on younger demographics. COVID has been positive for the group as greater health awareness has driven strong member growth, while delayed elective medical procedures have reduced expenses, delivering higher profits. Using long-run pre-COVID margins to forecast earnings rather than current elevated margins, the fund estimates the company is trading at a significant valuation discount to the market. The company has a strong track record of earnings growth and generates a very high return on capital. Macro tailwinds include a tax system that incentivises private health insurance and the sector's importance to the long-term sustainability of the Australian healthcare system given government funding constraints. The fund expects NHF to be a long-term holding.
quote: We added NIB Holdings (NFH) to the portfolio in April. It is a relatively well known Australian private health insurer, focused on younger demographics. Covid has been positive for the group as greater awareness of health care has driven strong member growth. Additionally many elective medical procedures have been delayed / cancelled. So strong revenue growth combined with lower expenses delivering higher profits. Many are concerned about a strong rebound in elective medical procedures impacting near-term profits. We agree this is somewhat likely however our investment process enables us to take a longer-term view. Using long run (pre-covid) margins to forecast earnings (not current high margins), we estimate the company is trading at a significant valuation discount to market. We also believe the company is a higher quality business than average. Large supportive macro tailwinds include i) a tax system which incentivises private health insurance membership, and ii) the sector's importance to the long-term sustainability of the Australian healthcare system given government funding constraints. At the company level it has a strong track record of earnings growth and generates a very high return on capital. We expect NHF to be a long-term holding in the fund.
